title: Git - Simply Explained
description:
If your project folders are named final, final-final and use-this-one, Git is the fix. This episode explains Git in plain English for beginners, makers and Microsoft 365 builders: commits, the staging area, branches, merges, conflicts and how GitHub and pull requests fit into a team workflow.
In this episode
00:00 – Git is your project history03:26 – The three local areas: working directory, staging area, repository07:17 – Branches, merges and conflicts10:46 – GitHub, the shared online repository13:55 – A Git-based team workflow15:55 – CI/CD, AI and the daily route
Key takeaways
Git is a local-first version control system that records deliberate, named checkpoints called commits, so you can see what changed and return to an earlier version.Changes move from the working directory through the staging area into the local repository, while branches let you work safely without disturbing the trusted main version.GitHub adds a shared remote repository and pull requests for review and automated checks, turning separate computers into one team workflow: work, stage, commit, push, review, merge.
Worth quoting
“So think of Git as your project's memory, not a magic undo button, and not a coding language. It's a system for creating deliberate, named checkpoints that you can inspect later” – Mirko Peters (03:10)
“Git is the tool that tracks your project history. GitHub is an online place where people can share that history.” – Mirko Peters (02:29)
